sph_interpretive_translation: Witnesses must be established in Vedic and Smritic conduct, free from greed and hatred, of noble birth, blameless, and adorned with austerity, charity, and compassion.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from scriptural alignment and spiritual discipline
Causation through purity of witness rather than external compulsion
Capacity-based responsibility rooted in consciousness maturity
Restoration logic via elevation of witness integrity
executable_legal_axioms: IF witness_status IS claimed THEN verify śrauta-smṛta observance = TRUE
IF lobha OR dveṣa detected IN witness THEN disqualify automatically
IF kulīnatva AND anindya conduct NOT present THEN witness capacity = null
IF tapas, dāna, dayā absent THEN witness truth-value weight = 0
IF all qualifiers met THEN witness integrity score = maximum
supreme_court_application: In the Supreme Court of Dharma, only those witnesses who demonstrate unbroken alignment with śruti-smṛti disciplines and exhibit absence of personal motive or bias shall be admissible. Their testimony carries full legal validity only when authenticated by tapas, dāna, and dayā — ensuring that consciousness purity underpins judicial knowledge.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality requires that a witness' inner state determines testimonial accuracy. Anupūrvaśaḥ establishes that greed or hatred distorts perception sequentially. Therefore, responsibility lies in cultivating witness integrity, not punishing falsehood. Truth emerges naturally where consciousness is purified; hence, no punitive framework is required.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Re-establish śrauta-smārta conduct for disqualified witnesses
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Encourage voluntary withdrawal if internal impurities arise
Capacity Restoration Pathway: Engage in tapas-dāna-dayā triad until qualified
Integrity Reintegration Cycle: Continuous self-assessment against greed-hatred tendencies
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: This law restores Dharma through pure witnessing, aligns reality with non-punitive consciousness jurisdiction, and affirms that only enlightened integrity serves as valid testimony.
